title: Electrical panel (breaker box)

parts.label: Panel door and cover
parts.looks: A grey or beige metal box on the wall with a hinged door; behind the door, a flat cover (dead front) with only breaker handles showing.
parts.normal: Cover in place with every slot filled or blanked.
parts.abnormal: Cover missing, an open slot showing the inside, rust on the box.

parts.label: Main breaker
parts.looks: The largest breaker, usually at the top, marked with a bigger number (100, 150, 200).

parts.label: Branch breakers
parts.looks: Rows of smaller breaker handles, each with a number (15, 20, 30).
parts.normal: All handles lined up in ON.
parts.abnormal: One handle in the middle (tripped) or OFF; discoloured or melted handles.

parts.label: Circuit directory
parts.looks: The paper list of circuits inside the door.
parts.abnormal: Blank: worth labelling, not a fault.

parts.label: Panel brand label
parts.looks: The maker's label inside the door or on the cover.
parts.abnormal: Some older brands are often flagged by inspectors for replacement; we only note the brand, never judge it on camera.

parts.label: Scorch or melting
parts.looks: Brown or black marks, bubbled or melted plastic.

parts.label: Exposed or loose wire
parts.looks: Bare copper or wires visible outside the cover.
parts.abnormal: Safety issue when visible without opening anything.

parts.label: Water staining
parts.looks: Drip marks or rust trails on or above the panel.
parts.abnormal: Safety issue if water is on the panel now.

faults.name: Tripped breaker
faults.evidence: One handle visibly out of line with the others. Resetting is the caller's choice; we never tell them to touch anything inside.

faults.name: Panel replacement candidate
faults.evidence: The brand label or age, read from the outside; quote the replacement estimate visit, it is not by itself an emergency.

hazards.label: Exposed wiring or open slots
hazards.threshold: Bare wire, an open knockout or a missing cover that exposes the inside of a panel that is installed on a wall.

hazards.label: Scorch or melting at the panel
hazards.threshold: Clearly visible brown or black scorch, or melted plastic, on a breaker or the cover.

hazards.label: Water on the panel
hazards.threshold: Water drops, a wet streak or a drip landing on the panel or its wiring.

may: Show the panel from the outside with the door open.
Step back so the whole panel is in view.
must_not: Remove the cover (dead front) or any screw.
Touch any wire or anything inside the box.
Stand in water near the panel.
Reset a breaker that trips again right away.

tour.open: Let's look at your panel. Open only the small door, nothing else, and stand back about two steps so I can see the whole panel. Please do not touch anything inside.

checkpoints.hint: Step back so I can see the whole panel and the wall around it.
Move a little closer to the top of the panel, where the biggest breaker usually is. Don't touch it.
Tilt down slowly along the rows of breakers.
Show me the paper list inside the door.
